Native Adventure action-interruption popup source grammar, DF 53.16

Actual Ghidra 12.1.4 C output is retained in pe-steam-ghidra-decompiled.c and
pe-classic-ghidra-decompiled.c, plus one C file per native owner. Original
instructions, bytes, finite literal operands, condition edges, switches and
CHAININFO fragments are retained alongside those sources. pe-images.tsv records
the actual configured PE identities, SHA-256 values and image paths. These are
offline source materials, not game observations or test results. This semantic
grammar describes those original sources; it is not itself Ghidra-generated C.

OWNER AND REACHABILITY

Steam PE:6a70a6d9:02711000; classic PE:6a70b91c:0270a000.
Steam populate 0x84ef40..0x84f51e; classic 0x84c7c0..0x84cd9e.
All five CHAININFO fragments of each populate owner are included. The vector
begins with a literal null pointer. Both native allocation sites then write
integer action type 3, never an adventure_optionst virtual table. They enumerate
eligible tiles in the 3-by-3 same-z neighborhood and directly above at z+1,
excluding the already held coordinate. Original availability predicates and
cached-position branches remain in the complete populate C and assembly.

The activation caller is Steam owner 0x7eed80..0x7f3ca2 at call 0x7f30d0;
it activates this popup only when the vector contains at least two entries.
The popup therefore has null plus one or more type-3 choices. The separate
77-class Adventure action chooser is not this popup's option hierarchy.

Renderer: Steam 0x8a68a0..0x8a6e61; classic 0x8a4120..0x8a46e1.
Input: Steam 0x8a6e70..0x8a7b1c; classic 0x8a46f0..0x8a539c.
Native switch/remap bytes follow input code and are retained by pe-switches.tsv,
not decoded as instructions. Every selector 0..27 has the native mapped target
that invalidates the matching old action. Ghidra legitimately folds this into
one destination. Scroll drag/update: Steam 0x8a7b40..0x8a7cc2; classic
0x8a53c0..0x8a5542. That owner supplies no prose.

FINITE TEXT AND FULL CAPTION GRAMMAR

TITLE := "Would you like to take an action?"
NULL_CHOICE := "Do not alter actions"

Each type-3 option stores signed 16-bit coordinate groups:
CURRENT := option+0x8/+0xa/+0xc
SOURCE := option+0xe/+0x10/+0x12
TARGET := option+0x14/+0x16/+0x18

TYPE3_CHOICE := VERB TILE " (" DIR(CURRENT,TARGET)
                [" from " DIR(CURRENT,SOURCE)] MEDIA ")"
VERB := "Hold " when TARGET.z <= SOURCE.z; otherwise "Hang from ".
The " from " group exists only when CURRENT and SOURCE differ in x, y or z.
The current populate owner writes CURRENT=SOURCE, but the caption supplier's
complete conditional branch is retained and its grammar must remain supported.
Non-null types other than 3 leave the output empty; populate cannot create them.

MEDIA := ["/Air"] ["/Water"] ["/Lava" | "/Magma"]
These three gates are independent, in this fixed order, and use SOURCE.
Air requires tile type in {1,32,35,42}, water depth<=6 and magma depth<=6.
Water requires water depth>0. Lava/Magma requires magma depth>0; tile flag bit
15 selects "Magma" when set and "Lava" otherwise. All gates and branches are
present in each complete interrupt-option-caption C and assembly.

TILE is the complete native terrain description at TARGET, with growth=false:
Steam supplier 0xe7d330; classic supplier 0xe782a0. The existing real Ghidra
sources and complete material suppliers are retained under
data/extracted/adventure-action-terrain, referenced by native-supplier-sources.tsv.
Terrain names contain material, construction, plant, feature and mod RAW fields;
they are semantic fields rather than a finite enumeration of generated names.

DIR := NW | SW | West | NE | SE | East | North | South,
       each optionally followed by /Below or /Above; or pure Below | Above | Here.
These are exactly 27 native direction outputs. Steam supplier 0x74f220 and
classic 0x74cc40 are already retained in the actual Ghidra sources under
data/extracted/adventure-action-menu; native-supplier-sources.tsv links them.

INPUT FAILURE ANNOUNCEMENT

FAILED_GRAB := "You fail to grab the " TILE "!"
Input builds it at Steam literal site 0x8a7883 and terrain call 0x8a78df;
classic sites are 0x8a5103 and 0x8a515f. This field is the same native terrain
description at the option's TARGET, growth=false. It is not an item caption.
All remaining input branches handle selection, pointer/key input, scroll,
action cancellation/commit, and successful or failed grabbing without adding
another finite text production in this popup's complete native owners.

NATIVE BYTE CLIPPING BEFORE DRAW

The renderer creates every complete caption, then compares its byte length
against available row cells. This is a separate clipping site from the 77-class
chooser. On the clipping path it resizes the std::string, inserts a NUL and,
when the retained length exceeds 3, overwrites the final three bytes with "...".
There is no native text wrapping in this path.

Steam compare 0x8a6d0e; branch 0x8a6d11 (72 7e) skips to 0x8a6d91.
The string-size/NUL block begins 0x8a6d24 and is 22 bytes; append-padding
call is 0x8a6d49. Dot writes are 0x8a6d62, 0x8a6d75 and 0x8a6d88.
List draw addst call 0x8a6d9f returns to 0x8a6da4; title addst call
0x8a6a86 returns to 0x8a6a8b.

Classic compare 0x8a458e; branch 0x8a4591 (72 7e) skips to 0x8a4611.
String-size/NUL block 0x8a45a4; append-padding call 0x8a45c9; dot writes
0x8a45e2, 0x8a45f5 and 0x8a4608. List draw addst call 0x8a461f returns
to 0x8a4624; title addst call 0x8a4306 returns to 0x8a430b.
pe-instruction-bytes.tsv preserves the exact original bytes for every instruction.
